text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today, continuing a downturn that's lasted two weeks. The main driver appears to be crude oil prices: US oil dropped to $96.16 per barrel, and Saudi Arabia's restoration of pipeline flows through the Red Sea to around 3.5 million barrels per day signals that supply constraints that had tightened markets are now easing. When oil prices fall, producers like ConocoPhillips face lower revenue per barrel, even if they pump the same volume.

The broader picture is one of improving global energy supply after recent disruptions. News of recovered export flows through both the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia's Red Sea route, plus Shell's commitment to expand Canadian LNG capacity, suggests markets are pricing in a more stable, plentiful energy picture ahead — the opposite of the tight supply environment that had supported higher oil prices earlier in the month.
